newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: UN's Annan said to offer Indo-Pakistan meeting.
newsitem.headline: UN's Annan said to offer Indo-Pakistan meeting.

text.p: Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan said on Wednesday that U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan had invited him and his Indian counterpart to a dinner meeting, the official APP news agency reported.

He told reporters on his return after attending a Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) meeting in New Delhi that NAM members and Annan were happy over the recent resumption of India-Pakistan peace talks after a three-year hiatus.

Khan, who met Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Wednesday, was quoted by APP as saying Annan, who was in New Delhi for the NAM meeting, had invited him and Gujral to dine with him in New York and hold talks during the next General Assembly session.
Earlier on Wednesday, Khan and Gujral held confidence-building talks in New Delhi amid rising hopes their rival nations will be able to defuse half a century of tensions.
The maiden meeting between Gujral and Khan marked the first talks since negotiations resumed last month after a three-year hiatus marred by diplomatic sniping and an insurgency in divided Kashmir.
The two nations, which have fought three wars, two of them over Kashmir, since independence in 1947, resumed high-level talks last month.
